name: qwen-code
title: Qwen Code
note: compaction: om's summary is handed back at the SessionStart after Qwen's (source compact)

name: qwenpaw
title: QwenPaw (formerly CoPaw)
manual: Console > Agent > MCP, paste the MCP client JSON
note: per agent; stored in that agent's agent.json

name: raycast
title: Raycast AI
manual: run the Install MCP Server command and fill in the stdio form

name: recursechat
title: RecurseChat
manual: Model page > New Model > New MCP Model

name: refact
title: Refact
manual: Refact settings > Integrations > MCP (stdio)
note: only project .refact/integrations/*.yaml documented; development moved to JegernOUTT/refact, Refact Cloud retired

name: roo-code
title: Roo Code
note: the global mcp_settings.json in stock VS Code's storage (Edit Global MCP opens it); with roo-cline.customStoragePath set, or in a VS Code fork, use om install --mcp-config on that file

name: rovodev
title: Rovo Dev CLI (Atlassian)
note: the file is whatever mcp.mcpConfigPath in ~/.rovodev/config.yml names (default ~/.rovodev/mcp.json); `acli rovodev mcp` opens it; disabledMcpServers in config.yml can keep it off

name: roxy
title: Roxy
manual: Settings > Add-ons > MCP Servers

name: seekchat
title: SeekChat
manual: Settings > MCP > add a server, type stdio, as one command line (om's path must have no spaces)

name: shinkai
title: Shinkai Desktop
manual: add an MCP server of type Command in the app's MCP servers settings
note: servers live in the node's SQLite database (Command/Sse/Http types)

name: slack-mcp-client
title: Slack MCP Client
manual: add it under mcpServers in the bot's config.json (the file --config names)

name: sourcegraph-cody
title: Sourcegraph Cody
manual: profile icon > MCP Settings, or add it under the "cody.mcpServers" key of VS Code's settings.json (needs the agentic-context-mcp-enabled flag on the instance)

name: swarmclaw
title: SwarmClaw
manual: MCP Servers panel > New MCP Server (stdio), then assign it to agents

name: sweep
title: Sweep AI (JetBrains)
manual: Shift Shift > Sweep Settings > MCP Servers > Edit MCP Config File (mcpServers JSON)
note: file path not documented; local servers only
source: https://docs.sweep.dev/mcp-servers (via search summary; host unreachable here)

name: tabnine
title: Tabnine (IDE and CLI)
note: Tabnine CLI's hooks (Gemini CLI style): AfterAgent hands om the prompt and reply, which it records itself, and PreCompress compacts; the CLI is deprecated after 2026-12-31 (docs.tabnine.com, Tabnine CLI hooks)

name: text-generation-webui
title: Text Generation WebUI (textgen)
manual: create user_data/mcp.json (mcpServers map, Claude Desktop format) in the install folder, then restart
note: file lives under the install directory, not a fixed user path; usable with om install --mcp-config <install>/user_data/mcp.json

name: tgpt
title: tgpt
note: found in source only (src/mcp/mcp.go), not in the README; ./mcp_config.json in the current directory wins; env is a KEY=VALUE list

name: theia-ide
title: Theia IDE
note: AI features must be on; restart, or run MCP: Start MCP Server

name: tome
title: Tome
manual: MCP tab > add server, and paste the command

name: trae
title: Trae
manual: Settings > MCP > Add > Add Manually, and paste it under mcpServers
note: Claude-style hooks: om records each prompt and reply itself (no transcript it reads); no compaction hook, so memory is the tool's and the session-start context

name: twinny
title: Twinny
note: VS Code user setting (flat dotted key, map by name); paths are VS Code stable's, other VS Code forks differ; servers restart when the setting changes

name: typingmind
title: TypingMind
manual: Settings > Advanced Settings > Model Context Protocol: run the npx @typingmind/mcp connector it shows, then Edit Servers

name: vercade
title: Vercade
manual: add it under mcpServers in the mcp.json the MCP_PATH variable names

name: vim-ai
title: vim-ai
manual: no native MCP; with the kracejic/vim-ai-provider-openai-mcp plugin set provider=openai-mcp and options.mcp=<path to a JSON server file> in the [chat] config
note: third-party provider, stdio only, early version; JSON file schema not documented

name: void
title: Void
note: Void is deprecated (README); file is reloaded on change

name: vtcode
title: VT Code
manual: in vtcode.toml (vtcode --version shows where) set enabled = true under [mcp] and add a [[mcp.providers]] table with name = "om", enabled = true, command and args as below

name: witsy
title: Witsy
note: close Witsy before installing (it rewrites the file); om's path must have no spaces

name: xum
title: Xum (formerly Mux, Coder)
manual: Settings > MCP, or in ~/.xum/mcp.jsonc under servers add "om": "<om> mcp --harness xum" (one shell command string; quote om's path if it has spaces)
note: each server value is ONE shell command string, not an object: quote the om path if it has spaces; also editable in Settings > MCP; older Mux used ~/.mux

name: y-cli
title: y-cli
manual: run y-cli mcp add, then list the server in a bot's mcp_servers

name: yume
title: Yume
manual: Yume runs Claude Code and uses its MCP servers: run om install claude-code

name: zencoder
title: Zencoder (VS Code)
note: VS Code's settings.json with comments is refused: then add it by hand; restart the IDE

name: zeroclaw
title: ZeroClaw
manual: add a [[mcp.servers]] entry (zeroclaw config set mcp.servers.NAME.command ...) and grant it to an agent through an [mcp_bundles.*] entry in agents.<alias>.mcp_bundles
note: a server alone is not granted to any agent; grants are per agent alias

name: zin-mcp-client
title: Zin MCP Client
manual: add it under mcpServers in mcp-config.json beside the zin-mcp-client script, or pass --config <file>
